text:
sara (support): opening thread for an escalation from a customer (they asked to stay anonymous here) — intermittent SSE sessions getting cut mid-event when routed CF -> NLB -> backend. They see partial event payloads and client reconnects, sometimes multiple reconnects before full message arrives. They attached a simple curl and a browser capture.

liam (oncall): curious if NLB is doing tcp proxy vs ALB http proxy. NLB usually preserves TCP but idle timeout can still be an issue if there's an idle timer on connection pools. Do we have any app logs / tcp traces?

sara (support): customer says they put Cloudflare in front (full proxy), then an NLB to our fleet (TLS passthrough). Browser devtools show events like: 
```
Event: data: {"id":"m1","text":"Partia"
Event: data: {"id":"m1","text":"l mess"
< connection closed by remote (FIN)
client: reconnecting, got tail only: "ge"
```
They tried curl too: 
```
curl -v -N --http1.1 -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  "https://svc.example.com/stream?topic=chat"
```

devin (runtime): interesting. Our runtime flushes per-token and sets TCP_NODELAY; we also call fflush on the HTTP library. With Cloudflare doing TLS termination then proxy to NLB, two possible problem spots: (1) CF buffers small writes (CF product docs mention buffering for origin fetch optimization), (2) NLB with TCP passthrough may have idle connection reuse semantics at the client side (CF) which can cause half-closed state if the origin closes due to app-level logic.

frank (infra): NLB passthrough should not mutate HTTP framing but we do have an idle timeout on our backends and connection trackers. NLB's default idle is 350s for TCP? (varies by provider). If the origin process closes the socket after sending final chunk the proxied connection can turn into a half-close where CF sees FIN on origin side and can re-use the downstream connection to client, leading to client-side truncated receipts.

liam (oncall): can we get a pcap from the backend during reproduction window (capture both server and host eth0)? Also ask customer to try a direct origin test bypassing CF (temporarily) to the NLB to see whether truncation persists.

sara (support): customer ok to test next morning. they asked for exact tcpdump commands and a minimal curl flag set to avoid CF buffering.\
devin (runtime): ask them to run: 
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/sse-trace.pcap host <client_ip> and port 443
```
And use curl with explicit no-buffer on both ends: 
```
curl -v -N --http1.1 --no-buffer \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
  "https://direct-nlb.svc/stream?topic=chat"
```
Also try `stdbuf -oL` on any local producer to avoid libc-level buffering in reproducer.

frank (infra): infra change proposal: temporarily enable connection-level tracing on the target hosts and bump our TCP keepalive/idle settings on the instance side: net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time=120, keepalive_intvl=15. We'll also enable verbose netstat logging for 2 hours.

infra-bot: infra-change planned: enable instance-side tcp keepalive tuning + packet-capture allowance on group tg-stream-01 from 2026-03-19T09:00Z -> 2026-03-19T12:00Z.

sara (support): scheduled with customer for 09:15 UTC. they will run curl, browser test, and upload pcap. asked whether we can confirm runtime behaviour on half-close: do we close after we send last chunk or keep socket open?\
devin (runtime): we leave stream open until client closes or until server-side send terminates. For event streams we typically send chunks and keep the connection open (idle). We do defensive flush per write. If app-level code does a socket close after last byte and the proxy sees FIN, proxies may forward FIN differently depending on connection mode.\
liam (oncall): other quick checks for customer: (1) set `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no` (some proxies respect that), (2) set `Cache-Control: no-transform` to discourage CF from altering payloads, (3) try using HTTP/2 vs HTTP/1.1 to compare (CF sometimes does h2->h1 conversion).\
sara (support): sending checklist to customer now. Also asked if we have any server-side logs linking to connection IDs we can provide to them so they can match pcap times.\
frank (infra): give them the instance IPs and ask to correlate with our load balancer logs (we'll collect flow logs + netstat). Also capture the trace-id header if present — we add `x-rd-trace` on responses.\
customer (via email excerpt): "We see many tiny packets (50-200B) spaced milliseconds apart, then a FIN from origin, and CF returns final ACK to client and closes. Behaves fine at low throughput but under parallel clients the truncation spikes."\
devin (runtime): that pattern screams Nagle + proxy coalescing + half-close. If CF collapses multiple upstream writes into a single downstream frame and then connection swapping happens, browser gets a partial JSON / truncated SSE data. Remediations (ordered):
1) Recommend customer configure Cloudflare route to bypass CF buffering for that path (page rule or origin settings). Cloudflare product docs: set `disable_chunked_encoding`/page rule to disable buffering.
2) If bypass isn't possible, have customer use a separate subdomain behind the NLB that is not proxied by CF (direct origin) for streaming clients.
3) Increase keepalive and idle timers on origin and proxy to ensure long-lived idle streams persist (we'll bump ours during the window).
4) As a fallback, make the server emit periodic heartbeat comments `: keepalive

liam (oncall): good list. action items: 
- sara: collect pcap + curl output + browser HAR from customer.
- frank: perform the infra tweaks during the window (tcp_keepalive change + logging) and share LB logs.
- devin: be on standby to triage pcap; if it's FIN after small packets that's the indicator.

sara (support): thanks all — will update here after they upload the artifacts. :thumbsup:
